speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand what's going on, can you describe the skin lesions for me? Specifically, how long have they been there, and are they itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the daycare exposure and the brother's recent chickenpox, are the lesions fluid-filled blisters, and do they appear in different stages of healing (some crusted, some vesicular)? Also, has the child had any fever or seemed generally unwell?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. The presence of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is highly characteristic of Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
